notes: One typescript sheet, with handwritten page number - 5 -, handwritten appended/interline references, Greek mathematical fill-ins, and six handwritten digits in the final citation. Archive sheet number 69 is recorded only as a comment. No title, date, salutation or signature is present. The sixteen reference entries concern pages 11–17, followed by two labelled identities and an unfinished continuing sentence. Authorial questions/doubts are preserved: a reference should be supplied in Exp.V; the definitions might make sense for C merely connected, ending 'ou est-ce que je me canule ?'; '(SGA ou EGA ? )'; an already cited fact is used 'sans référence'; 'propre et lisse' may suffice; and the author questions the inference of smoothness from geometrically regular fibres without flatness. The single-n canule is independently confirmed, with no linguistic correction. The lower and upper rules of handwritten IV and III are live notation, not deletion strokes. No authored deletion, diagram, or independent drawing was identified. Small isolated background specks without a text or graphic attachment are not assigned punctuation. H is description-only, so h_reading is null and diff_h false throughout. Its page wrapper is archival metadata. The final two identities were read sign by sign; they were not proved or checked against any external theorem. No mathematical claim has been silently repaired.
math_reading_decisions: The first line has ordinary single-struck typed K and T in both terms. Its first filled round point is raised and its second is lowered: K^{\bullet}(T) and K_{\bullet}(T), agreeing with C. These are points, not primes or stars.
All inline mathematical capitals C, S and X were checked separately in their occurrences. Their single typed outlines support ordinary capitals; none has an independently doubled alphabetic stroke.
The first curve-point subscript reads os by its low oval o and s; the second remains \unsure{l|1}s. Both suffixes are below their x, without commas or an intervening sign.
The handwritten IV and III in the interline p.13 reference carry both upper and lower rules. The typed IV in the EGA reference and the typed V in the concluding reference do not carry such rules.

The two initial Greek signs are live handwritten \psi, with the typed lower suffixes i and i+j respectively. Their central long descenders and two raised arms distinguish them from a plain Y. No arrow occurs in either display.

The three lowered handwritten crossed forms in the right-hand class symbols are \chi. Each has a crossing oblique stroke descending leftward below the lower hooked terminal. These three places were independently cropped once; no deletion or alternative alphabet was established.

The displays retain all typed c exponents i and j, variables x and y, nested parentheses, equals signs, and the minus signs and factorials exactly as C gives them: (-1)^{i-1}(i-1)! in (i), and (-1)^{i+j-1}(i+j-1)! in (ii). The exponent j has a descender; i has a separate dot. Both display labels and both final commas are present.

The concluding citation reads V 6.5.3 et 6.6.4. V, et, both parentheses, the separating points and the final comma are typed; all six digits are handwritten fill-ins. This is a change in recorded material state, not a change to the citation numbers.

All numbered prose references and their punctuation were read from the two halves, including (3.1), EGA IV 2.8, both occurrences of 2.12, the handwritten cf. 7.16, and 7.13.6. No proof or computation was performed.
